method: SORTED BY EYE FROM THE CONTACT SHEETS ALONE, BEFORE ANY METRIC WAS OPENED, and the sheets are the same geometry the round sort used (4x3 at 460 px a cell, tools/battle_place_sheets.py defaults). Each cell is the shipped `decide` command-step frame of a REAL battle at the same 62 census landing cells, photographed through the stage's own snapshot() with NOTHING driving the camera (tools/battle_decide.mjs --mode=census). The only numbers seen before this file existed were the four progress columns the capture prints per site, exactly as in sort.json; census-*.json was not opened until both verdict sets were written. Nine sites were re-opened at full resolution because the sheet cell was ambiguous (after: s011 s020 s034 s046; before: s004 s017 s019 s039); two of those changed pile (before s019 and s039, bad -> acceptable) and the rest confirmed.

rubric.good: all bodies read immediately as separate figures; what is behind them differs from them in value or is open; the ground plane reads; no single surface owns the frame
rubric.acceptable: readable but compromised — one side of the cast is low-contrast, or one surface owns half the frame, or the place is odd but legible
rubric.bad: a body is effectively lost (inside foliage, or at its background's own value, or in near-black), or one surface owns the frame with nothing else in it, or the party is in a hole / on a roof / behind clutter

departure: ONE DEPARTURE FROM THE RUBRIC'S LETTER, and it is about the LENS rather than the PLACE. sort.json's 'good' says ALL FOUR BODIES read as separate figures. The `decide` shot is a 27 mm two-shot on the deciding character, so the two party bodies overlap into one silhouette at MOST sites in BOTH arms — a fixed property of the shot, present everywhere, and scoring it would have measured the camera and called it placement. Party-on-party overlap is therefore not counted as a defect here; every other clause is applied as written. Also noted and NOT scored: the shipped command menu is a DOM overlay that snapshot() cannot see, so a real player sees this frame with a menu box over its lower band.
arm: BEFORE the sun refusal (BattleWorld.PLACE.on = false, i.e. ?bplace=0)
